$comment: Machine form of SPEC_UV_CANONICALIZATION.md. A consumer that cannot read the prose can still check that the form it implements is the form the seed declares.

artifactCanonicalDigest.reason: canonical document bytes are a serialization question, not a value-graph question

encoding.number: ["number","<16 lowercase hex digits of the big-endian IEEE-754 binary64 bits>"]
encoding.object: ["object",[[<JSON key literal>,<encoded value>],...]] with keys sorted by UTF-8 byte order

rules.typeTagsAreLoadBearing: a tagged number and a tagged string can never collide, and neither can an empty object and an empty array
rules.numericModel: one type only: IEEE-754 binary64, encoded as its bit pattern rather than as a decimal rendering
rules.float32Widening: float32 widens to binary64 exactly; no requantisation step exists
rules.nonFinite: NaN and infinity are rejected; there is no fallback value
rules.keyOrder: UTF-8 byte order, with a UTF-16 code-unit tie-break that only applies to ill-formed input
rules.arrayOrder: preserved. Where order is not semantic the producing spec sorts before encoding; the form never sorts on the producer's behalf

digestEnvelope.rationale: an algorithm-qualified digest makes a future algorithm change visible in every artifact that carries one

provenance.liftedFrom: packages/world/src/canonical.ts in the sealed legacy oracle
provenance.reason: a digest produced against this specification and a digest produced by the sealed implementation must agree, so the differential oracle of block 11 stays meaningful
